history.en: The location of Kalamadhava is not identified by Sircar or Green Message. Popular lists place it in a hill cave by the Son river at Amarkantak, where the Son and the Narmada rise. No specific shrine has been identified, so the map pin marks Amarkantak town. About 2 km south of the Narmada temple, at Sonmuda, two ponds named Sona and Bhadra join to form the Sonbhadra (Son) river, which falls in a waterfall.

story.en: According to the Puranas, Sati, the daughter of Daksha, gave up her life in the fire of her father's sacrifice after he insulted her husband Shiva. Grieving, Shiva carried her body across the world until Vishnu's discus divided it, and each place where a part fell became a Shakti Peetha. Tradition holds that Sati's left buttock fell here.

en: The site of this pitha is uncertain.
Amarkantak lies where the Vindhya and Satpura ranges meet.
Sonmuda, the source of the Son, has a waterfall said to be about 300 feet high.

timings.en: No official timings are published; check locally before visiting.

nearestRail.en: Pendra Road (about 43 km) and Anuppur (about 75 km).

bestSeason.en: Pilgrims visit Amarkantak through the year.
